name: Fushi Face Lifter

lead: The Fushi Face Lifter is a V-shaped chin strap tool made of stretchy rubber or silicone. It loops over the head and under the chin, and it is marketed to lift the lower face, define the jawline and reduce the look of a double chin while worn.

The appearance payoff is a tighter-looking jaw and neck line during wear, as the band holds soft tissue up and back. It belongs to a broad category of V-line straps sold by many sellers, and no published trial has tested whether such straps change facial shape after they are removed.

paras: Users put the strap on at home, typically for short periods while relaxing, and some sellers also market overnight versions. Users often pair it with facial massage, exercises or skincare. Any look change is described as appearing while the strap is on.

Common concerns are skin irritation, pressure marks and discomfort from tight straps, and overnight wear can interfere with comfort. Manufacturer claims about permanent reshaping have not been tested in published studies.

chain: Elastic strap holds tissue up and back
Neck and jaw line looks tighter while worn
angle.text: The strap gives mechanical lift to the soft tissue under the chin while it is worn. Wearers use it for a defined jaw and neck line in the mirror or photos. Lasting change after removal is claimed by sellers but untested.

lead: The Fushi Face Lifter is a V-shaped chin strap made of elastic rubber, sold to lift the lower face and sharpen the jaw and neck line. It sits in the larger family of V-line face-slimming straps sold under many brand names.

People wear straps like this at home for a visibly tighter jaw line while they are on, and some pair them with facial massage, exercises or neck skincare. Sellers describe the effect as lifting skin and soft tissue toward the ears and temples. A review of a similar TikTok-popular strap described wearing it after skincare, starting with 30 to 60 minute sessions, and noted a temporary all-day tightening when combined with a firming neck cream.[1]

No published clinical study has tested this product or V-line chin straps for lasting changes in facial contour. Dermatologist Abigail Waldman has commented publicly that overnight wear is not matched by gravity pulling on the face during sleep.[1]
infobox: Comparable chin straps are listed at about $10-14 online[1]
At home, worn for set periods

paras: The strap forms a V that cups the chin and runs up past the cheeks to anchor over the head or ears. Similar bands are described as wide, stretchy and fastened with adjustable wings. Many are washable and reusable, and some are marketed for overnight wear.[1]

Face straps are discussed among jawline and double-chin gadgets alongside massage tools and exercise devices. Users typically describe changes in the mirror while the strap is on; a reviewer of a similar strap reported no permanent change in jaw or chin shape.[1]
The reviewer of a similar strap reported skin marks and discomfort, including fit that was initially too tight.[1] Users with sensitive skin typically choose softer materials.
